result:
The proposed solution gives no derivation. It only says "through systematic enumeration" and asserts 108, so I checked it against a lower bound and against what I remember of this problem.

A 4×6 rectangle splits into four 2×3 blocks, and each block has 2 tilings by two L-triominoes. That gives at least 16 distinct tilings. In any tiling, two neighboring triominoes already allow 3·2 = 6 colorings. This suggests a lower bound of roughly 16·6 = 96 before counting the other tilings, and in practice many tilings have more colorings per tiling than that minimum. Reaching exactly 108 would need an average of about 6.75 colorings per tiling, which is implausibly low given the constraints.

I also recall the known answer to this competition problem (HMMT) as 1296, not 108. I did not enumerate the tilings and colorings myself, so this rests on the bound and on my recollection of the answer.

VERDICT: REJECT
